description: Number patterns, rules, and adding series

lessons.title: Number Patterns
lessons.intro: A sequence is a list of numbers that follow a pattern. Spotting the pattern lets you predict what comes next!
explanation: 2, 4, 6, 8, ... each number is 2 more than the last.
Patterns can add, subtract, double, and more.
lessons.rule: A sequence follows a rule from one term to the next.
lessons.tip: Find what changes between the numbers.

steps.text: Look at the gap between terms.

lessons.title: Counting Up
lessons.intro: Many sequences simply count up by a fixed step.
explanation: The step stays the same each time.
lessons.rule: A fixed step makes a counting sequence.
lessons.tip: Add the step to get the next term.

lessons.title: Steps of Three and More
lessons.intro: The step can be any number, not just one or two.
explanation: Check the gap is the same each time.
lessons.rule: Any constant step gives a steady pattern.
lessons.tip: Confirm the gap before predicting.

lessons.title: Doubling Patterns
lessons.intro: Some sequences multiply instead of add — they grow much faster.
explanation: Doubling makes numbers shoot up quickly.
lessons.rule: A doubling sequence multiplies by 2 each time.
lessons.tip: Check: is it adding or multiplying?

lessons.title: Growing Gaps
lessons.intro: In some clever sequences the gap itself grows.
explanation: Each gap is one bigger than the last.
The next gap is 5, so the next term is 16.
lessons.rule: Sometimes the gap increases by a pattern.
lessons.tip: Look at the gaps between the gaps.

lessons.title: Arithmetic Sequences
lessons.intro: An arithmetic sequence adds the same amount each time — this amount is the common difference.
explanation: Find it by subtracting one term from the next.
Add the common difference to extend the sequence.
lessons.rule: Arithmetic sequence = fixed common difference.
lessons.tip: Difference = any term minus the one before.

steps.text: Subtract to find the common difference.

lessons.title: Finding the Difference
lessons.intro: The common difference can be found anywhere in the sequence.
explanation: A negative difference means the sequence decreases.
lessons.rule: Common difference can be positive or negative.
lessons.tip: Decreasing sequences have negative differences.

lessons.title: Decreasing Sequences
lessons.intro: When the common difference is negative, each term is smaller.
lessons.rule: Subtract the difference for a decreasing sequence.
lessons.tip: Watch the sign of the difference.

lessons.title: Extending Forward
lessons.intro: To find the next term, add the common difference to the last term.
lessons.rule: Next term = last term + common difference.
lessons.tip: Keep adding the same step.

lessons.title: Finding Far Terms
lessons.intro: You can jump ahead by using the position and the difference.
explanation: 5th term of 3, 8, 13, ...: start 3, add 4 four more times -> 23.
This avoids writing out every term.
lessons.rule: Term = first + (position - 1) x difference.
lessons.tip: Count the gaps, not the terms.

quiz.hint: Each term is 2 times its position.

lessons.title: Finding the Rule
lessons.intro: A rule connects a term's position to its value, so you can find any term instantly.
explanation: Rules save you from listing everything.
lessons.rule: A rule links position to term value.
lessons.tip: Test your rule on the first few terms.

lessons.title: Rules with Plus
lessons.intro: Many rules multiply the position and then add a number.
lessons.rule: Rule form: (step x position) + start adjust.
lessons.tip: Substitute the position carefully.

lessons.title: Testing a Rule
lessons.intro: Always check a rule by trying it on known terms.
explanation: It should match every given term.
If one fails, the rule is wrong.
lessons.rule: A correct rule matches every term.
lessons.tip: Test at least two terms.

lessons.title: Rules from Words
lessons.intro: Real situations give rules too.
explanation: Chairs = 2 x tables + 1: 10 tables give 21 chairs.
Turn the words into a rule.
lessons.rule: Translate word situations into position rules.
lessons.tip: Find the 'per' amount and the start.

lessons.title: Rule Master
lessons.intro: Use rules to find far-off terms with ease.
explanation: Rule term = n x n: 6th term is 36.
lessons.rule: Apply any rule to find distant terms.
lessons.tip: Write the rule, then substitute.

lessons.title: Missing Terms
lessons.intro: Sometimes a term in the middle is missing — use the pattern to fill the gap.
explanation: 2, ?, 6, 8 ... the step is 2, so the missing term is 4.
Find the step from the known terms.
lessons.rule: Use the common step to find a missing term.
lessons.tip: Check both neighbours of the gap.

steps.text: Step 2 means the missing term is 4.

lessons.title: Filling Counting Gaps
lessons.intro: In a steady counting sequence, the missing term sits exactly between its neighbours.
explanation: The gap value is the average of its neighbours.
lessons.rule: A missing counting term = average of neighbours.
lessons.tip: Add neighbours and halve.

lessons.title: Gaps with Bigger Steps
lessons.intro: The same idea works for any constant step.
explanation: Confirm the step from the known terms.
Add the step to fill the gap.
lessons.rule: Find the step, then fill the blank.
lessons.tip: Check your answer fits both sides.

lessons.title: Doubling Gaps
lessons.intro: If the sequence doubles, the missing term is found by doubling or halving.
explanation: Double 12 to get 24, which doubles to 48.
lessons.rule: In a doubling sequence, multiply/divide by 2 to fill gaps.
lessons.tip: Check the term after fits too.

lessons.title: Tricky Gaps Master
lessons.intro: Harder sequences hide the gap inside a growing pattern.
explanation: Look for growing gaps or special numbers.
lessons.rule: Spot growing gaps or square patterns for hard gaps.
lessons.tip: Write the gaps underneath the sequence.

lessons.title: What is a Series?
lessons.intro: A series is the SUM of the terms of a sequence — adding them all up.
explanation: The sequence lists; the series totals.
lessons.rule: A series is the sum of a sequence's terms.
lessons.tip: List the terms, then add carefully.

steps.text: Write the terms of the sequence.

lessons.title: Adding in Pairs
lessons.intro: A neat trick: pair the first and last terms to add quickly.
explanation: Each pair has the same total.
Multiply the pair total by the number of pairs.
lessons.rule: Pair outer terms to add a long series fast.
lessons.tip: Pairs of equal sums speed things up.

lessons.title: Sums of Even and Odd
lessons.intro: Adding only evens or only odds gives tidy totals.
explanation: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared!
lessons.rule: Sum of first n odd numbers = n squared.

lessons.title: Savings and Totals
lessons.intro: Series appear whenever we add up amounts over time.
explanation: The running total is the series.
lessons.rule: Total saved = sum of each period's amount.
lessons.tip: Add step by step or in pairs.

lessons.title: Series Master
lessons.intro: Combine your tricks to sum any simple series.
lessons.rule: Use pairing and patterns to sum series fast.
lessons.tip: Check with a rough estimate.
